site.name: codekite
site.summary: codekite-clone Fictional cloud CI/CD service "CodeKite CI" marketing site, focused on the pricing-page usage calculator. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: hero (YAML code example on the right), 3 feature cards, CTA to pricing | | `pricing.html` | Main page: 3 plan cards (Free / Team / Enterprise) + usage calculator (three slider+number pairs linked two-way: build minutes / concurrency / storage + ARM / macOS / GPU runner checkboxes); right-side sticky monthly total + recommended-plan badge + line-item cost breakdown; below: 16-row plan comparison table; 10-question FAQ accordion; trusted-logo row; 4-column footer | | `docs.html` | Placeholder quickstart page (one YAML example) |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full codekite system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The codekite pricing page has functional sliders/number inputs and cost updates, but key issues include unresponsive CTA buttons, non-functional FAQ accordions, small mobile tap targets, and missing input labels. Coverage is partial (27%), with untested navigation links and some interactables.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full codekite system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start with the landing page (index.html), then move to the pricing page (pricing.html) to interact with the usage calculator and plan cards, followed by the docs page (docs.html). Each page will be explored in both desktop and mobile viewports, with a focus on interactables, layout warnings, and user flows.
assumptions: The site has three main pages (index, pricing, docs) with the pricing page being the most interactive.
The pricing page has a usage calculator with sliders and checkboxes that need to be validated.
Layout warnings (small tap targets, missing labels) should be checked for usability.
risk_hotspots: pricing.html (usage calculator with missing input labels, small tap targets)
all pages (small tap targets for navigation links)

phases.title: Explore Landing Page (index.html)
phases.objective: Validate the landing page's interactables, layout, and flow to pricing/docs.
key_checks: Click navigation links (Product, Pricing, Docs, Sign in, Start free trial) and check for responsiveness.
Click 'See pricing' and 'Read docs' buttons and verify navigation.
Check layout warnings (small tap targets) for usability in both viewports.
exit_criteria: All main interactables on index.html are tested, navigation to pricing/docs works, and layout warnings are noted.

phases.title: Explore Pricing Page (pricing.html) - Plan Cards
phases.objective: Validate the plan cards (Free, Team, Enterprise) and their CTAs (Get started, Start trial, Talk to sales).
key_checks: Click 'Get started' (Free plan), 'Start trial' (Team plan), and 'Talk to sales' (Enterprise plan) and check for responsiveness.
Verify the plan details (features, pricing) are clear and interactive elements work.
Check layout warnings (small tap targets, missing input labels) for the plan cards section.
exit_criteria: All plan card CTAs are tested, plan details are verified, and layout warnings for plan cards are noted.

phases.title: Explore Pricing Page (pricing.html) - Usage Calculator
phases.objective: Validate the usage calculator (sliders, checkboxes, total cost breakdown) and its responsiveness.
key_checks: Interact with sliders (build minutes, concurrent builds, storage) and check two-way binding (slider <-> number input).
Toggle checkboxes (Linux ARM, macOS, GPU runners) and verify cost updates.
Check layout warnings (missing input labels, small tap targets) for the calculator section in both viewports.
Verify the recommended plan badge and cost breakdown update correctly.
exit_criteria: Usage calculator interactables are tested, cost updates work, and layout warnings for the calculator are noted.

phases.title: Explore Pricing Page (pricing.html) - Comparison Table & FAQ
phases.objective: Validate the plan comparison table and FAQ accordion for usability and clarity.
key_checks: Scroll through the plan comparison table and check for clarity of features across plans.
Open/close FAQ accordion items and verify responsiveness.
Check layout and interactability of the trusted-logo row and footer.
exit_criteria: Plan comparison table and FAQ are tested, trusted-logo row and footer are verified.

phases.title: Explore Docs Page (docs.html)
phases.objective: Validate the docs page's content and interactables.
key_checks: Click navigation links (Product, Pricing, Docs, Sign in, Start free trial) and check for responsiveness.
Verify the YAML example and quickstart content is clear.
Check layout warnings (small tap targets) for usability in both viewports.
exit_criteria: Docs page interactables are tested, content is verified, and layout warnings are noted.

phases.title: Cross-Check Viewports & Recovery Paths
phases.objective: Verify all critical flows (pricing, docs, navigation) in both desktop and mobile viewports, and check recovery paths (back navigation, error handling).
key_checks: Repeat critical checks (navigation, calculator, plan CTAs) in mobile viewport.
Test back navigation (browser back button) after each navigation and verify state retention.
Check for console/network errors during all interactions.
exit_criteria: All critical flows are verified in both viewports, back navigation works, and no new errors are found.

coverage_targets.pages: visit all three known HTML pages (index, pricing, docs) in both viewports.
coverage_targets.features: exercise all visible controls (navigation links, buttons, sliders, checkboxes, accordions) per key page.
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks (navigation, calculator, plan CTAs) on mobile viewport to validate responsiveness and layout.

notes: Focus on the pricing page's usage calculator as the primary flow, with adjacent pages (index, docs) for context. Layout warnings (small tap targets, missing labels) should be prioritized for usability critique.

findings.user_goal: Start a trial or talk to sales
findings.problem: CTA buttons (e.g., 'Start trial', 'Talk to sales') lack visible feedback (navigation, modal, or confirmation) when clicked, making it unclear if actions are recognized.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Start trial' (Team plan) and 'Talk to sales' (Enterprise plan) resulted in no URL change, modal, or text update. The 'Get started' button updated the URL with a hash but no further feedback.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may abandon the flow due to uncertainty if their action (e.g., starting a trial) was successful, reducing conversion rates.
findings.suggestion: Add immediate feedback (e.g., navigation to a confirmation page, a modal, or a success message) to confirm CTA actions are processed.
findings.source_hint: pricing.html: Start trial, Talk to sales

findings.user_goal: Expand FAQ accordions to get answers
findings.problem: FAQ accordion items fail to expand when clicked (timeout errors), preventing users from accessing help content.
findings.evidence: Multiple attempts to click the first FAQ item (e.g., 'Do unused build minutes roll over?') failed due to timeouts, with no expansion or content revealed.
findings.why_it_matters: Users seeking clarification on pricing or usage rules cannot access critical information, increasing support requests or user frustration.
findings.suggestion: Fix the accordion's interactivity (e.g., ensure JavaScript binds click events, check for z-index issues, or improve element accessibility) to allow expansion.
findings.source_hint: pricing.html: FAQ accordion items (ux-28, ux-29, etc.)

findings.problem: Small tap targets (e.g., navigation links, checkboxes, CTA buttons) on mobile violate accessibility guidelines (e.g., <44px height/width), making interaction difficult.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings show tap targets like 'CodeKite' (118x28px), 'Pricing' (47x21px), and checkboxes (13x13px) are below mobile guidance (44px minimum).
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users may struggle to tap elements accurately, leading to frustration and increased error rates.
findings.suggestion: Increase tap target sizes (e.g., expand button/link dimensions, add padding) to meet 44px minimum height/width for mobile interactions.
findings.source_hint: pricing.html: mobile viewport (e.g., navigation links, checkboxes)

findings.user_goal: Interact with form inputs (sliders, number fields)
findings.problem: Form inputs (sliders, number fields) in the cost calculator lack visible labels or aria-labels, reducing accessibility for screen reader users.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings and DOM summary show input fields (e.g., build minutes, concurrency) have no associated labels, placeholder text, or aria-labels.
findings.why_it_matters: Visually impaired users cannot understand the purpose of inputs, leading to errors in estimating costs or configuring usage.
findings.suggestion: Add visible labels or aria-labels to all form inputs (e.g., 'Build minutes per month', 'Concurrent builds') to clarify their purpose.
findings.source_hint: pricing.html: cost calculator inputs (ux-7, ux-8, etc.)

findings.problem: Many navigation links (e.g., 'CodeKite', 'Docs', 'Pricing' in docs.html) remain untested, with unknown responsiveness or functionality.
findings.evidence: Coverage gaps show 27% feature coverage, with untested links like 'CodeKite' (docs.html), 'Docs' (docs.html), and 'Pricing' (docs.html) not exercised.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may encounter broken navigation, reducing trust in the site's reliability and hindering exploration of other pages (e.g., docs, product info).
findings.suggestion: Test all navigation links to ensure they navigate to the correct pages and have responsive feedback (e.g., URL updates, visual state changes).

findings.problem: The cost calculator's 'ARM runners (~25% of minutes)' and similar line items lack clarity on how the percentage is applied (e.g., 25% of which minutes?), causing confusion.
findings.evidence: The cost breakdown shows 'ARM runners (~25% of minutes)' but does not specify if it's 25% of total build minutes or a subset, leading to ambiguity in cost estimation.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may miscalculate costs due to unclear percentage definitions, leading to unexpected bills or reduced trust in the pricing model.
findings.suggestion: Clarify the percentage calculation (e.g., '25% of total build minutes') in the cost breakdown labels to improve transparency.
findings.source_hint: pricing.html: cost breakdown (e.g., ARM runners line item)
